title: Braid
summary: BRAID, verb transitive [Old Eng. brede.] 1. To weave or infold three or more strands to form one. 2. To reproach. [See Upbraid.] BRAID, noun A string, cord or other texture, formed by weaving together

inlines.v: BRAID, verb transitive [Old Eng. brede.] 1. To weave or infold three or more strands to form one. 2. To reproach. [See Upbraid.] BRAID, noun A string, cord or other texture, formed by weaving together different strands. 1. A start. BRAID, adjective Deceitful. Chaucer used the Saxon word brede, to deceive. This is the figurative sense of braid
